note: Dollar cost per centerline mile of street made all-ages, by facility type, in millions of dollars. Read by scripts/school-budget-strategies.py (central, to rank picks by children per dollar) and scripts/school-budget-value.py (low, central, high, to cost each strategy). Budgets at approval, not final spending; dollar years differ by source and are not adjusted except where 'why' says so. No SFMTA or SFCTA unit-cost table by facility type was found.

separated.label: Separated bike lane, quick-build (paint, posts, some concrete)
separated.applies_to: North Star blocks drawn Separated; any block on a collector, arterial or other non-residential street that a school link or off-plan pick upgrades
separated.source: Five SFMTA quick-build budgets at Board approval, design and construction, per corridor (centerline) mile: 17th St $0.89M, Mid-Valencia $1.38M, Winston Dr $1.51M, Frida Kahlo Way $1.57M, Beach St $1.61M; Mid-Valencia $2.39M with its stated unfunded $900,000. Per-mile figures derived (budget / length). Table and links in notes/bike-network-2026-09/2026-09-29-brp-gap-areas.md.
separated.why: Central is the median of the five (rounded). High is Mid-Valencia with escalation. A concrete build costs far more: the Central Embarcadero memo gives $8-12M for about half a mile ($16-24M/mi); not used, since the plan and SFMTA's recent bikeways are quick-builds.

calmed.label: Traffic-calmed shared street (Slow Street or neighborway: diverters, humps, signs, stencils)
calmed.applies_to: North Star blocks drawn Shared; residential blocks (DataSF 3psu-pn9h classcode 5, or 0) a school link or off-plan pick upgrades
calmed.source: SFMTA Board, 2022-12-06, Item 14 (Slow Streets Program), staff report printed p. 13: 'Slow Street improvements generally consist of lower-cost spot treatments such as traffic calming elements, signs, and pavement stencils, with an average cost of implementation of approximately $200,000 per mile.' https://www.sfmta.com/reports/12-6-22-mtab-item-14-tc-amendment-slow-streets-program. High: Bushell et al., Costs for Pedestrian and Bicyclist Infrastructure Improvements, UNC HSRC for FHWA, 2013, printed p. 12: bicycle boulevards 'typically range from approximately $200,000 to $650,000 each', https://www.pedbikeinfo.org/downloads/Countermeasure%20Costs_Report_Nov2013.pdf
calmed.why: Low is SFMTA's 2022 average. Central adds about 25% for 2022 to 2026 prices and for diverters a busier street would need [assumption]. High takes UNC's upper per-project figure as per mile, a project being about a mile [assumption]. The staff report does not say centerline or directional; a Slow Street is one street, so read as centerline [inference — mine].

path.label: New shared-use path, or a walk path off any street made rideable
path.applies_to: North Star blocks drawn Shared-use Path; walk edges on no street centerline that a school link upgrades
path.source: Bushell et al. 2013 (above), Path table, 'Multi-Use Trail - Paved', per mile, 2012 dollars: median $261,000, average $481,140, maximum $4,288,520 (42 observations), PDF p. 26.
path.why: No SF per-mile figure. Peer figures times 1.5 for 2012 to 2026 prices [assumption]: low the median, central the average, high the maximum.

car_free.label: Car-free street (an existing road closed to through traffic)
car_free.source: Sunset Dunes, about 2 miles of the Upper Great Highway, reported at $1.2M to $1.97M: secondary reporting only.
car_free.why: No primary SF figure. The plan's Car-free blocks are a small share of any strategy's miles, so this range moves no total much.

per_link_fixed_musd.why: Sensitivity only, not in the central costs. A short school link built as its own project carries planning and design that a per-mile rate spreads over a longer corridor: 17th St's $615,000 included $210,000 that was not construction (notes/bike-network-2026-09/2026-09-29-brp-gap-areas.md). [assumption]
